properties.description: Warfarin is an anticoagulant used to treat and prevent blood clots in conditions like deep vein thrombosis.
Warfarin can increase the risk of bleeding due to its anticoagulant effects.
Warfarin inhibits the VKORC1 gene product, which is involved in the clotting process.
Metformin is the first-line treatment for managing Type 2 Diabetes.
Metformin activates AMPK, which plays a role in glucose metabolism.
Lisinopril is an ACE inhibitor used to treat hypertension.
Lisinopril inhibits the ACE gene product, reducing blood pressure.
Sertraline is commonly prescribed for Major Depression.
Sertraline acts on the serotonin pathway to exert its antidepressant effects.
Ibuprofen is used to relieve joint pain associated with conditions like osteoarthritis.
Ibuprofen inhibits COX-2, reducing inflammation and pain.
Aspirin is used in certain patients to reduce the risk of heart attacks in heart failure.
Aspirin can cause gastrointestinal bleeding due to its antiplatelet effects.
Methotrexate is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug used for rheumatoid arthritis.

Insulin can be contraindicated in patients with certain types of hypothyroidism.

Gabapentin is used to manage chronic pain conditions.
Gabapentin has sedative properties that can help with insomnia.
Prednisone is a corticosteroid used to manage inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.
Prednisone can cause weight gain as a common side effect.

Levothyroxine acts in the thyroid hormone pathway to regulate metabolism.
